Find your expression.

Black hair. Different textures. Individual style.

Save an idea for your next visit. These are style references, not separately priced services. Ask your barber which booking and finish are right for you.

Taper fade

A focused blend at the temples and nape, leaving more length through the sides. Ask for a low, mid or high taper.

Skin fade

The shortest finish: a blend from bare skin into the hair above. Fade height and top length are separate choices.

Waves & line-up

Close, even length to show the wave pattern, with a crisp outline. Discuss cutting with the grain.

Afro & temple taper

Keep the volume and natural texture, with a shaped outline and a controlled taper at the temples.

Textured cut & beard

Work with curl, density and face shape for a considered balance between the top, sides and beard.

Short natural taper

A shaped curl silhouette with tapered sides and nape. Bring a reference for the top length and finish.

Know your grade.

A small number. A different finish.

Choose a grade to see the approximate length it leaves. The shortest grade, the fade height and the length on top are three different choices—talk through each with your barber.

Your length reference

Skin

Bare-skin finish

Skin is a finish, not a guard number. Usually achieved with a foil shaver or razor after the clipper work.

Approximate Wahl guide-comb lengths: 0.5 ≈ 1.5 mm, 1 ≈ 3 mm, 1.5 ≈ 4.5 mm, 2 ≈ 6 mm, 3 ≈ 10 mm, 4 ≈ 13 mm. Length varies with equipment, lever position and technique. A 0.5 guard is not 0.5 mm. Guide-comb reference ↗

Tools of the art.

Precision has more than one instrument.

Clippers

Remove length and blend with guide combs.

Detail trimmer

Refine line-ups, necklines and beard edges.

Scissors

Shape the top, balance volume and refine texture.

Straight razor

Create precise edges or a close shave when suitable.

Shaving & finish

A foil shaver takes a fade close; brush and lather prepare a wet shave.
